inventory_evidence.full_context:
**21 Write sequential.** Writes the record at the DMA address at the FCB's
`CR` and moves on. It takes a new allocation block or a new extent when the
record falls in one (`src/cpm/bdosrec.asm:22-207`). Returns 0 on success.
Returns 1 when the directory has no entry for a new extent or when the close
of the extent it leaves finds no entry for it. Returns 2 when the drive is
full. After a 1 the FCB stays on its extent with `CR` at 128, so a later
write, once an entry has been freed, makes the extent the FCB needs
(`src/cpm/bdosrec.asm:119-175`). A block taken for a write that then fails
stays in the FCB's map. A later successful close publishes it in the entry
(`src/cpm/bdosrec.asm:733-767`). An FCB with the read-only attribute set gives
the `File R/O` error (`src/cpm/bdosfile.asm:430-445`).

Older cards hold their services in files of type `.DRV` and this ROM doesn't
load them. The CCP takes `GLCD.DRV` as the name of a program and prints it
with a question mark, so a board with the graphics LCD keeps its console on
the serial terminal until a usable driver is installed and selected. A

boot without a card driver. The web page reports an old GLCD driver for a
GLCD display choice, as Appendix I describes (`host/card.mjs:26-48`).

reviews.reason: So directly introduces why a dropped directory block alone cannot give Write lost next boot.

inventory_evidence.full_context:
The cached changes in dropped lines are lost and the next warm boot has
no such lines left to retry. A directory line is dropped when its write
or preceding data flush fails. The BDOS reports `Bad Sector` at once. If
only the directory write failed, its dropped block leaves nothing for the next
warm boot to retry, so that failure alone gives no `Write lost`. The data blocks
that failed stay dirty in the cache. Another close or flush can retry them.
The warm boot after the recovery key writes them again and gives `Write lost`
if writes still fail (`src/cache.asm:292-345`, `632-651`). The file
that was being written needs writing again, once the card is put right and the
board reset.

reviews.reason: And directly coordinates missing drives/table-sum fields with the host volume-count limit.

inventory_evidence.full_context:
A card's minor version sets three things. A 1.0 card has no drives field and
no table sum, and `tecvol` gives it at most 8 volumes. A 1.1 card may have up
to 127, may give a number of drives and has the table sum
(`tools/lib/container.mjs:76-80`, `tools/lib/container.mjs:140-148`).
`tecvol create` makes a 1.1 card when it is given more than 8 volumes or
`--drives`, and a 1.0 card otherwise. The ROM rejects a 1.0 card of more than
8 volumes with code `24h` (`src/vol.asm:113-151`). It treats any minor
version other than 0 as 1.1 (`src/vol.asm:171-175`).

reviews.reason: So directly connects the earliest volume start with unused table blocks remaining outside volumes.

inventory_evidence.full_context:
Block 0 holds the header and descriptors 0 to 14, at offsets 32 to 511. A 1.1
card with more than 15 volumes goes on in blocks 1 to 7, 16 descriptors to a
block. With block 0's 15 that gives the limit of 127
(`tools/lib/container.mjs:33-42`, `format/format.json`). Descriptor `i`, for
`i` of 15 or more, is in block `1 + floor((i − 15) / 16)`, at
`32 × ((i − 15) mod 16)` within it. No volume can start below block 8, so
blocks 1 to 7 remain outside every volume, whether or not the table uses
them.

reviews.reason: So directly relates the 128-byte record size to four records per card block.

inventory_evidence.full_context:
Both geometries use 128-byte records and 64 records per track
(`format/format.json`, `geometries`). Record `r` starts at byte `128 × r`
in the volume's payload, so four records share a 512-byte card block.
Neither geometry has reserved tracks, sector skew or a directory check
vector. The card is not removable media in CP/M's sense.

inventory_evidence.full_context:
Each directory occupies four allocation blocks. G8M's 512 entries of
32 bytes occupy 16 KiB, or four 4-KiB blocks. G1M's 256 entries occupy
8 KiB, or four 2-KiB blocks. Those four blocks come from the volume's
2,048 allocation blocks on G8M or 512 on G1M.
